formation.explanation: RawNode.Propose or serialized Node proposal handling reaches the current role. Followers forward to a known leader unless forwarding is disabled; candidates drop. The leader assigns current-term consecutive indexes, appends unstable entries, queues its own append response for persistence and broadcasts append messages anchored by previous index/term. A follower checks that anchor, appends only noncommitted conflicting suffix, bounds propagated commit to the matched extent and queues its reply through persistence. Term-filtered successful replies update peer Match. Active voter majority order statistics, or the minimum of both joint majorities, select a candidate index; leader commit advances only when that entry has its current nonzero term. Rejections, heartbeat-driven retries and snapshot fallback resynchronize lagging peers. Ready exposes committed entries only beyond the issued application frontier and blocks while a snapshot is outstanding; async delivery additionally requires locally stabilized entries. Advance or local apply response advances internal applied and frees budget. Node explicitly permits early Advance while external application runs, with inter-Ready application order left to the caller; this differs from the asynchronous response-after-apply contract. Client proposal return is only admission/Step outcome and can precede or never lead to commitment.

context.explanation: Ticks or Campaign enter hup, which checks promotability and unapplied configuration changes. Pre-election does not raise term; a real campaign increments term and records self Vote, with self response delayed for persistence. Vote grants check vote availability and log freshness. Candidate response type and active voter quorum determine win/loss. A winner resets progress and appends an empty current-term entry. Higher-term ordinary messages, election loss and configured quorum inactivity demote; lease/pre-vote exceptions are explicit. Transfer blocks new proposals, catches up the selected nonlearner and prompts a fresh election; timeout aborts transfer. Startup reconstructs log bounds and configuration from caller Storage, loads saved term/vote/commit and becomes follower. Snapshot restoration rejects obsolete or ineligible snapshots, fast-forwards a matching committed boundary, or installs snapshot history and configuration; a pending snapshot prevents promotion. Configuration activation uses validated simple changes or joint enter/leave, preserves progress for retained peers, initializes new progress at zero and handles configured leader removal. Application progress can initiate automatic joint exit. The configuration scan reads from applied+1 to committed, while existing-leader, local voter eligibility and pending-snapshot checks independently gate campaigning. A passed scan alone is not evidence that a new leader can obtain a quorum.

connection.explanation: Term/role reset discards votes, peer progress and safe-read acknowledgment tracker while preserving local log and committed frontier. Self progress is initialized from local lastIndex, including potentially unstable inherited entries, so Match must not be equated with a fresh durable acknowledgment. Leader formation appends a current-term empty entry; commit requires the selected entry term to equal the leader term, preventing the old self frontier alone from authorizing new-term commitment. Active membership changes reinterpret retained progress and can re-evaluate commit; new peers begin Match=0. Stale-term replies do not advance leader support or stabilize entries. Local append completion additionally matches entry term/index; a later current-term append message can reconfirm outstanding writes. Committed state and application acknowledgments survive term changes: apply responses are term zero, snapshot completion can be processed despite stale term, and applied uses a monotonic maximum. Pending pre-commit read requests survive reset but enter the new read-only mechanism only after current-term commitment; existing safe-read acknowledgment state is reset. Recovery starts as follower with caller-supplied persisted prefix and configuration, not restored leadership. The accepted follower append history is represented by the unstable overlay until replacement writes are reflected safely in Storage. Storage-completion validation controls when queries fall through to Storage: message raft term and entry term/index are distinct context checks. This persistence boundary feeds both term-based support validation and election log freshness. Runtime application acknowledgments also connect completion with formation and authority: synchronous Node.Advance advances internal applied through a queued apply response, while ApplyConfChange separately changes the active tracker. The pending configuration proposal guard and unapplied-configuration campaign scan consume internal applied. Thus acknowledgment is not itself evidence of configuration activation; caller ordering determines whether these meanings coincide.

grounding.derivation: Node.ProposeConfChange states that configuration changes are dropped unless the leader is certain there is no prior unapplied configuration change. Node usage step 3 includes ApplyConfChange; step 4 explicitly allows Advance any time after persistence step 1, while preserving application order. Accordingly the selected Node contract permits finite early acknowledgment without treating a not-yet-activated and not-rejected configuration as applied for admission. A new configuration must not be accepted during that interval. This is a one-way rejection requirement, not a requirement that later proposals must succeed.
grounding.applicability: Public synchronous Node; configuration validation enabled; caller fully persists each Ready before Advance, eventually invokes ApplyConfChange in order for each accepted committed configuration, and does not reject the pending configuration. No dependency on peer health determines rejection.
